chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He was asked about a man who had sheep and cattle, and he would catch the live one from them, separate it, and separate the dead one. Then the dead one and the live one mixed together. What should he do with it? He said: 'Sell it to one who considers the dead one permissible and eat its price, and there is no objection to that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when live and dead livestock mix together in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istihsan* (preference) regarding the impurity of the carcass (*maytah*) when mixed with live livestock. The Imam’s ruling to sell to *Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book) who consume their own slaughtered meat highlights the distinction between the physical impurity of the dead animal and the ritual purity of its monetary value (*thaman*), a key concept in Usuli fiqh. This method allows the owner to liquidate the mixed herd without needing to separate the specific impure carcass, relying on the buyer’s consumption of the whole group as a form of purification through exchange.
